A bicycle gear system allows riders to adjust the effort needed to pedal based on terrain, speed, and personal preference. It consists of a front chainring (usually one or two large sprockets near the pedals) and a rear cassette (multiple sprockets of varying sizes on the rear wheel). The system uses a chain to transfer power from the pedals to the rear wheel.

When you pedal, the chain moves around the front chainring and the rear sprocket of your choice. The gear ratio—the relationship between the number of teeth on the front chainring and the rear sprocket—determines how much force is required and how far the bike travels per pedal revolution.
